indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the two pieces together run backwards

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
Albert Camus, the French novelist of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A quiet French author reminisces about trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns both pieces round together, not just the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumachs are shrubs and small trees of the genus Rhus, grown for their autumn colour.

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the contempt word goes round the letter for left

parts.note: to spit is to show contempt

explanation.surface: The political Left sneers at austerity cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the definition (departed, split) but gives only L.
explanation.definitionFit: Splits and cuts are both divisions made in something, nouns or verbs alike.

parts.note: Theresa May was Home Secretary when the puzzle appeared in 2014
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: The Home Secretary's border policy has caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Secretary is the UK minister responsible for policing and immigration; in 2014 that was Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder, a straightforward synonym for chaos.

indicators.note: to labour is to work, and the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: David Cameron following a Labour government is accused of a formal lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party but is the anagram signal, as in working; 'after' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial dress or duties are formal, done according to ritual and protocol.

clue.text: Person robs poor to make cut?

definitions.text: Person robs poor to make cut?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters cut into the person word, splitting it open

parts.note: one is a pronoun for an unspecified person

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A chancellor robbing the poor to make spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer who led austerity cuts in 2014, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints the Chancellor of 2014, known for cutting public spending, which hit poorer people hardest.

definitions.note: noun sense, the working or functioning of something

indicators.note: the opening word squeezes the other piece inside it

parts.note: to open is to start
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A start has been made to squeezing a proportion of the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The operation of a machine is its working or functioning, as in 'in operation'.

indicators.note: off is read as wrong or awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled
cut means the name loses its tail letter

explanation.surface: A writer cuts Boris Johnson off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks BORIS to BORI, and 'off' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, something one writes with, hence a writer.

indicators.note: leading puts the short word in front of the other piece

parts.note: re means on or concerning
to train a camera or gun is to focus it

explanation.surface: Policy focuses on leading schools once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to school or teach someone again in new skills.

clue.text: Sick feeling question avoided, it's simple

definitions.note: describes the quality of the noun, the state of being simple

indicators.note: avoided means the question abbreviation is left out

parts.note: queasiness is nausea

explanation.surface: A sick feeling, a question dodged: it's simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiness is the quality something has when it is simple to do.

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for wife is dropped

parts.note: a solicitor is a kind of lawyer

explanation.surface: A solicitor sleeps alone, his wife missing from the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology or gardening a bed is a stratum or thickness of material, a layer.

clue.text: Thinks too much of Gove (prat) — he's sacked heads about reading?

indicators.note: about means these trimmed words go round the reading letter
sacked heads means each of the three words loses its first letter

parts.note: he's is short for he is, so its letters are H, E and S
R is reading, one of the three Rs of basic education

explanation.surface: Michael Gove, sacked as Education Secretary, was a prat who rated himself too highly.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading GOVE, PRAT and HE'S gives OVE, RAT and ES; these go about R. Gove was moved from the UK education brief in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate someone is to rate or think too highly of them.

clue.text: The split, without a majority, it could turn to red or blue

definitions.text: it could turn to red or blue

indicators.note: without means outside, so the informer word wraps round the majority word

parts.note: to split on someone is to inform on them, to rat
most means a majority

explanation.surface: A split coalition without a majority could turn red (Labour) or blue (Conservative).
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics red is Labour and blue Conservative; the definition is the dial on a heating control, turned towards hot or cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat dial is often marked red for hotter and blue for colder settings.

clue.text: "Perhaps we give money to poor now?" (Shapps, surprisingly)

definitions.text: Perhaps we give money to poor

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Grant Shapps, Conservative chairman, surprises by suggesting giving money to the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant Shapps was Conservative Party chairman in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawnshops lend cash against pledged goods, often to people short of money.

clue.text: Time to deteriorate? Quite, in a way that might be naïve

definitions.text: in a way that might be naïve

parts.note: to rust is to decay or deteriorate
quite can mean fully or completely

explanation.surface: Time for things to deteriorate? Quite, says a naïve observer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with complete trust can be innocent or credulous, which is a naïve manner.

clue.text: Drop off in calls after bank's closure — protection for consumers rolled into these?

definitions.text: protection for consumers rolled into these?

indicators.note: after places the calling pieces behind the bank letter

parts.note: to drop off is to nap

indicators.note: closure means the final letter of the word

parts.note: rings means telephone calls

explanation.surface: Phone calls drop off after a bank closes, and consumer protection is folded in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: napkins, which protect diners (consumers of food), are rolled up into these.
explanation.definitionFit: Napkin rings hold rolled table napkins, the cloth that guards an eater's clothes.

clue.text: Supplies spin round seller in US

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin
O is round in shape
vender is the American spelling of vendor, a seller

explanation.surface: Supplies are spun round a seller in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is food or provisions, a store of supplies, especially fodder.

clue.text: US warehouse guy and soldier after part for gun

indicators.note: after sends the soldier word second, behind the gun part

parts.note: the stock is the butt of a gun
a man is a soldier, as in men under orders

explanation.surface: An American warehouse worker and a soldier go after a gun part.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a stockman is someone in charge of stock in a warehouse.

indicators.note: head to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a reserve is a store kept back

explanation.surface: Can you head to the pound store?
explanation.walkthrough: A pound store is a British shop where everything costs one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To can fruit is to preserve it in a sealed tin.

clue.text: Act while describing series of holes in changes of policy

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: as means while
a round of golf is a series of holes

explanation.surface: An act that goes through a series of holes in changing policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of tracing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnaround is a reversal of direction, so a political U-turn.

clue.text: It might make polls, we hear? Con: missing last three

definitions.text: It might make polls, we hear?
definitions.note: polls sounds like poles, which may be made of this cane

indicators.note: the final three letters of the deceiving word are dropped

parts.note: to con is to bamboozle or trick

explanation.surface: Pollsters admit the Tories are three short at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'poles' said aloud, as bamboo makes poles; Con also hints at the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo canes are a common material for garden poles.

clue.text: Clarke perhaps backing a vote against African

parts.note: Ken Clarke is the veteran Conservative politician, one example of a Ken

indicators.note: backing means read backwards

parts.note: nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: Ken Clarke is perhaps backing a vote against an African motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya in East Africa.

indicators.note: ignoring means the hospital letter is left out

parts.note: a chase is a hunt

explanation.surface: Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt ignores a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was UK Health Secretary in 2014; 'Hunt' is just the pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors speak of a patient as a case under their care.

indicators.note: contains means the sheet word holds the jumble inside it

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters are spread around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fliers are handed out; a sheet holds ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' jumbles the fliers, and 'contains' sets that jumble just after the first letter of the sheet word.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, teasing banter, a gentle form of mockery.

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the words hold the plant inside

explanation.surface: Baroness Warsi is permitted a house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sayeeda Warsi was a Conservative minister who resigned in August 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant grown for its fibre.

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the other answer is used

parts.note: the answer to 14 across, the table accessory

explanation.surface: The Lord's letters, partly referred to elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: INRI, initials of the Latin for Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews, was inscribed on the cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin initials placed above Christ on the cross are the Lord's letters.

indicators.note: balls is read as a mess, cockup, so the letters get scrambled

explanation.surface: Ed Balls says Eric Pickles is mad, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls (Labour) and Eric Pickles (Conservative) were 2014 politicians; here 'Pickles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinade food is to steep or pickle it in a flavoured liquid.
To lobby is to press politicians; a lobby is also a hall at the entrance of a building.

clue.text: More poor in northeast, back on dole, have had it, right?

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: back on means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: to have had it is to die

explanation.surface: Poorer people in the northeast are back on the dole and have had it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, meaning poorer or in greater want.

parts.note: to lay is to place
down is soft fluffy pile, like feathers or nap

explanation.surface: Surrender your seat and sit on a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down arms or office is to surrender or give them up.
